recipes.name: Barbecued Pork Kebabs
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 pound) boneless pork loin, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
10 bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes

steps.text: Whisk the sugar, soy sauce, onion, garlic and black pepper together in a large bowl. Add the pork and toss to coat. Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours. Overnight is best if possible.
Preheat an outdoor grill for high heat, and lightly oil the grate.
Thread the pork onto the soaked skewers. Cook on the preheated grill until the pork is no longer pink in the center, 3 to 5 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Barbecued Pork Kebabs
raw_recipe.description: This Filipino pork kebab recipe is great for outdoor parties, especially picnics. The pork needs to marinate at least for 2 hours.

review.reviewBody: Great marinade, pork was juicy and flavorful. I didn't make the kabobs, but grilled a whole pork tender loin, cut into about four pieces. Took about twice as long to cook.

Definitely a hit. I tried this for Christmas lunch. Did the marinate and left it overnight and added bell peppers and white onions to my kebabs. I also added paprika to the original recipe and used garlic and onion powder instead of whole garlic and onions. To grill I slow cooked then glazed with my bbq sauce. Kids, friends and family all loved it.

7.2.18 These kebabs were simply delicious. Only change I made was cutting back the amount of sugar and sub’ing Truvia® (personal taste preference here). I used pork tenderloin and marinated for about 8 hours. I often find that marinades with soy sauce end up with the meat tasting just like soy sauce, but that wasn’t the case here. I used pork tenderloin, and the pork flavor was the star. My pork cubes were about 1-1/2” to 2”, they were grilled for a total of 6 minutes, and they ended up slightly overdone. In the future, I’m thinking probably 4-5 minutes max to get that nice pink color and tender pork. Regardless, they still were devoured!

Delicious. I made this a few weeks ago for a group of 20 and it was a huge success.
I did add a tap of smoked paprika (just because) to the marinade and started the skewers off on the smoker for a couple of hours as we were in no hurry and then finished them off on the bbq until the inside temperature of the meat was at 145deg and then let them rest for 5 mins before serving.
It was so good I am making it again today.
These kebabs were very good. I added pineapple chunks between the pork when I put them on the skewers. I did these in oven at 375 for 15 minutes per side and they came out perfect. Very tasty.

This was a deliciously easy recipe! Made a couple changes to make it a little healthier. Used the juice from a can of pineapple slices, reduced sugar to 1/3 cup & used low sodium soy sauce. Made separate skewers with the pineapple, onions, bell pepper & cherry tomatoes and dipped each in the marinade before cooking. Turned out fab!

Very Tasty.Added 1/4 cup 7 up. Used 1/2 cup of white sugar,juice from 1/4 of lemon,a pinch of pepper flakes and 2tsp of canola oil to the mix.Marinated it over night.Great weeknight meal with the make ahead pork bbq.

Wonderful recipe! Of all the times I've made kabobs, I've never tried them with pork. We've been missin' out! I marinated overnight, using the recipe with 3/4 c. sugar rather than a full cup. We used metal skewers rather than bamboo. The flavor was great, and it paired really nicely with 'Brazilian Grilled Pineapple', 'Trees, Seeds and Beans' from AR and grilled green beans. Definitely a recipe worth repeating.
Very tasty, extremely tender and moist. I alternated with pineapple on the skewer. With definitely make again.

This is FANTASTIC. My husband says it's the best pork he's ever had, and I'm inclined to agree. Subbed brown sugar Splenda for the sugar. I used boneless country style pork ribs and trimmed the fat off of them before marinating because that's what I had on hand. Will absolutely be making this one again and again!
I loved this - it was so good. I did double the garlic and alternate on the skewers with fresh pineapple. Delicious - everyone really liked it.
Simple. Easy. Tasty! :-)

Wonderful and easy marinade. I did not bother with skewers as it was just me for dinner. I simply cut a small pork loin in to chunks, marinated about 3 hours, cooked low and slow on Kamado Joe. Delicious!
Great, easy recipe. Will definitely make these again.
I marinated tri tips instead of pork and grilled the kebabs over a fire on our camping trip. They were a hit!

I would make it again. I did not have time to let soak for 2 hours so left some aside to baste as cooking. They turned out GREAT! I would recommend people try this. I will add a touch of heat next time to the mix though.

Made this last night and my husband and I absolutely loved it. Had a busy day so only marinated for about 3 hours but the pork was still really full of flavor. Will definitely make this again. The only change I made was using half regular soy sauce and half low sodium soy sauce.
I let the meat marinate in the refrigerator for about 24 hours and they came out tender and delicious.
Needed more salt; flavor mild after 1.5 hours. Mild flavor that would go with a variety of sides.
Changed absolutely nothing and was amazed by these kebabs! Been waiting for an excuse to make them again!
